articles.title: The AI Adoption Blind Spot: How Fake AI Tools Put Enterprises at Risk

articles.title: Node.js Releases Security Updates to Fix High-Severity TLS, DNS and Brotli Vulnerabilities
articles.summary:
Node.js has released security updates for its 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x branches to address ten vulnerabilities, including four high-severity flaws affecting DNS lookups, TLS certificate checks, and Brotli decompression. The supplied release details identify 26.12.1, 24.22.1, and 22.23.4 as the patched versions. The most serious potential outcome is remote code execution through the Brotli decoder. […]

articles.title: China-Linked Hackers Turn Trusted Windows Applications Into Backdoors to Steal Credentials
articles.summary:

The group, tracked as BRONZE SANDCASTLE, places malicious files beside legitimate software, allowing familiar programs to run attacker-controlled code without changing the original application. articles.title: PHP Releases Emergency Patches for PHP2Shell Flaws Threatening Millions of Web Servers
articles.summary:
PHP has released emergency security updates for two critical vulnerabilities that could let unauthenticated attackers run code on vulnerable web servers. Tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, and collectively called PHP2Shell, the flaws affect PHP’s handling of memory during web requests. articles.title: APT28 Hackers Open Secret SSH Tunnel Into NATO Country’s Naval Shipbuilder Network
articles.summary:
Russian cyberespionage group APT28 used the Hookedge backdoor to reach a naval shipbuilder’s network in a NATO member state, steal login material and set up a hidden SSH tunnel. The intrusion lasted at least two months, according to a report by Symantec’s Threat Hunter Team. The report does not name the shipbuilder or the country. […]
